heading: Copy suppression may improve calibration by reducing copying overconfidence
definition: copy suppression makes the model less overconfident in naive copying, improving calibration.
summary: Evidence for improved calibration comes only from the original GPT-2 Small study, without independent testing in a pretrained language model. A toy sorting study found the opposite confidence effect: its suppressing head lowered entropy.

suggested_status.by_scale: R0 for GPT-2 small, from the original only (counts: V3.studies_by_size lists both studies as 'not stated'). Toy: one test by another group (arXiv:2501.18666), limits_scope, with the confidence effect in the opposite direction (head lowers entropy). No study at 1-10B, 10-100B or >100B.
suggested_status.reason: counts: V3.studies_tested 2. The original arXiv:2310.04625 (T1, no verdict by rule) reports one figure-only row: L10H7's direct effect decreases overconfidence in GPT-2 small, dataset not stated (r13). The other test, arXiv:2501.18666 (T3, a one-layer 2-head list-sorting toy), gets limits_scope: ablating its suppressing head leaves accuracy at 100%, raises loss slightly and raises entropy (r2-r4). counts: V3.verdicts.supports.studies 0, V3.verdicts.limits_scope.studies 1, V3.verdicts.challenges.studies 0, V3.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original 0. No independent study tests V3 on a pretrained language model. The toy result comes from a different setting with a limits_scope verdict, not a failed replication in GPT-2 small.
suggested_status.open_questions: An independent ablation of L10H7, or of a copy-suppression head in another pretrained LM, that measures a named calibration metric on an unselected distribution. This would move V3 to R2 if the improvement reproduces, or towards C if calibration does not improve. Also open: whether the head lowers confidence specifically where naive copying would be wrong; why the toy head lowers entropy while the original reports that L10H7 raises it; and whether any effect survives in larger models or after instruction tuning.

source.title: Copy Suppression: Comprehensively Understanding a Motif in Language Model Attention Heads
source.authors: Callum McDougall; Arthur Conmy; Cody Rushing; Thomas McGrath; Neel Nanda

original_result.setup: The authors ablated the direct output of L10H7 in GPT-2 Small.
original_result.result: They report that L10H7 decreases overconfidence; removing its direct effect shifts the model from net overconfident to net underconfident. Numerical values were not reported.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

wording_issues.phrase: copy suppression makes the model less overconfident
wording_issues.issue: The statement names no model or head. The original's Figure 13b caption reports reduced overconfidence from L10H7 in GPT-2 small (r13: figure-only, dataset not stated), although the checker notes an inconsistency with the accompanying ablation prose. In the one-layer, two-head toy list-sorting transformer, ablating the copy-suppressing head raises output entropy while accuracy remains at its 100% baseline (r3, r4). Entropy also increases after the other head is ablated. The suppressing head therefore increases confidence in this setting, reversing V3's confidence direction. The original also reports that L10H7 and other negative heads increase entropy (Appendix D, Fig. 13a, outside the rows).

The original explicitly defines and evaluates a calibration-curve-based overconfidence metric under direct-output ablation of L10H7 in GPT-2 small (Appendix D; r13). Numerical effect sizes and the evaluation dataset are not stated there. The toy list-sorting model reports loss, accuracy and Shannon entropy, without a named calibration metric. Accuracy is 100% both with and without the suppressing head (r3). Mean-ablation slightly increases loss, with no exact value reported (r2); this loss benefit from the intact head alone cannot determine whether it reduces overconfidence. The calibration wording therefore needs to retain the original's specific model, head and metric rather than treating the toy loss result as evidence of improved calibration.

method_sensitivity.what: In the toy 2-head sorting transformer (Dδ≈2.2), suppressing-head mean-ablation slightly raises loss (r2), but loss alone cannot determine reduced overconfidence: r2 is cannot_determine for V3, rather than partial. Accuracy is 100% before ablation and remains unchanged afterward (r3: cannot_determine). Entropy increases after either head is ablated; the suppressing head therefore increases confidence (r4: reversed for V3's confidence direction). Entropy alone does not establish worse calibration. The verdict remains limits_scope.

method_sensitivity.factor: Training data distribution, training stage and head count
method_sensitivity.what: The toy study reports that whether copy suppression emerges depends on the training data's gap distribution (its mean and variance). The head's specialisation also changes across training stages and with the number of heads. The V3 rows are from one setting only: 2 heads, Dδ≈2.2, after copy suppression has emerged.

method_sensitivity.factor: Sample selection, metric and input approximation in the original
method_sensitivity.what: The original paper reports that its results depend on three choices: the behavioural sample (top 5% by L10H7 effect), KL divergence versus loss-based metrics, and an idealised versus a more faithful input approximation. The pack does not say whether its V3 row (r13, dataset not stated) uses the top-5% sample.
